children: Norwegian telecommunications provider Telenor said Denmark's defense procurement agency entered a framework agreement to procure secure high-frequency communication systems from its subsidiary KNL.

KNL has developed high-frequency communication systems that operate independently of external infrastructure and provide an encrypted connection that it says also remains stable under jamming and other electromagnetic interference.
With the deal, Denmark becomes the third Nordic country after Sweden and Finland to join KNL's Nordic Defence Cooperation agreement, a pact which facilitates joint Nordic procurement.
To date, three orders have been publicly announced under the framework deal, with a combined value of around 23.5 million euros ($27.3 million).

The agreement with Denmark comes shortly after KNL was appointed as an approved supplier under the U.K.'s eight-year, 4.7 billion-pound ($6.37 billion), framework agreement for tactical communication systems, allowing it to compete for individual orders as they are tendered.
The company is also in discussions with several other North Atlantic Treaty Organization countries about further cooperation, it added.
